source.snippet: I live in France and work in Switzerland as a cross-border worker (frontalier). My salary is taxed at source in Switzerland. I'm considering opening a Pillar 3a account and contributing the maximum before December 31, but I'm not sure whether I can get any tax benefit from it in my situation. (2026-11-13)

problem_statement: Cross-border workers (frontaliers) living in France and employed in Switzerland cannot easily determine how Swiss Pillar 3a pension contributions interact with their dual-country tax obligations, leaving significant potential tax savings unrealized.
target_segment: French residents employed in Switzerland (frontaliers) earning CHF salaries who pay Swiss source tax and French income tax simultaneously.
notes: Frontalier population is ~200k workers. No clean tool exists for modeling Swiss/French dual-tax scenarios around Pillar 3a. A paid advisory service or SaaS calculator ($50–$200/year) targeting this niche has a clear buyer: someone actively deciding whether to contribute before a year-end deadline. High urgency and recurring annual need.
